name: Kennedy Lewis Investment Management
summary: Kennedy Lewis Investment Management manages Millrose and runs a separate private land-banking business with its own capital (Fund III, Fund IV and Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co, 'KLRES'), built from 2021 around a team that came from Domain. It signs builder commitments (New Home/Landsea, Dream Finders/Beazer, Taylor Morrison's Yardly, JPI) and then allocates them, so far mostly to Millrose; the August 2026 amendment to Millrose's management agreement loosened the rules on how deals are split with its private vehicles. Private-fund pricing and book size are not public; Millrose's non-Lennar yield (about 10.8%) is the best public proxy.

facts.fact: Proxy for Kennedy Lewis pricing via its public vehicle: Millrose's weighted average yield on non-Lennar agreements was about 10.8% in Q3 2026 (10.6% in Q2), guided to about 11% in Q4; the Lennar master program is cited at 8.5%; the Dream Finders preferred carries a 12% dividend.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

facts.fact: The New Home commitment letter names the fee stack (Initial Option Fee, Monthly Option Fee, Termination Fee, Asset Management Fee and a Minimum Project Return) but puts every number in a separate fee letter that was not filed. Kennedy Lewis's rates to builders in its private funds are not public.
facts.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

facts.fact: Template terms from Kennedy Lewis's 2025-05-12 commitment letter for a $700 million land bank to The New Home Company ('Project Lakeland'): up to $600 million funded at closing plus up to $100 million for horizontal development; Kennedy Lewis buys the properties, grants homesite options and pays development cost up to a guaranteed contract sum under construction agreements; no option term over 72 months; builder may stretch a takedown schedule by up to 20% before closing and take three quarterly deferrals per project.
facts.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

facts.fact: Same letter, risk protections: properties are grouped into pools of at least four projects; a builder walk-away on one option lets Kennedy Lewis terminate the rest of that pool (cross-termination), while builder's total payment obligation per pool is capped at $20 million; aggregate takedown price must be at least 105.25% of the closing commitment amount; builder pays diligence costs and expenses even if the deal does not close; funding was conditional on at least $650 million of sponsor equity.
facts.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

facts.fact: Scale with Lennar before and around Millrose: Hunterbrook reports that Lennar and Kennedy Lewis began a land-banking partnership in 2021 and that Millrose's investor presentation cites '$4.5B+' of land-banking transactions between the two since 2022. Kennedy Lewis has not published a total for dollars, lots or number of builders in its private strategy.
facts.source_title: Hunterbrook Media, 2026-10-02

facts.fact: Hunterbrook, quoting the Millrose prospectus, reports that Lennar picked Kennedy Lewis as Millrose's manager without a competitive selection process and that Kennedy Lewis served as Lennar's unpaid strategic adviser on the spin-off's structure and contracts; it dates the Richman-Lennar relationship back about two decades (he covered Lennar as a Goldman Sachs high-yield analyst).
facts.source_title: Hunterbrook Media, 2026-10-02

facts.fact: Millrose's FY2025 10-K states that Kennedy Lewis acted as Lennar's strategic advisor while the Lennar agreements were prepared and that it had no prior experience managing a public company.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 / Item 1A

facts.fact: The FY2025 10-K places the asset-servicing arm's staff in Scottsdale, Arizona and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (Kennedy Lewis HQ New York; other offices Miami and Geneva). The part of that filing read in this run did not name the servicer's leader.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 / Item 1A

facts.fact: Millrose's FY2024 10-K lists Kennedy Lewis itself among the key competitors in the land-banking market and warns that Kennedy Lewis manages land-banking entities that compete with Millrose for opportunities and resources. The glossary names two: Fund III (Kennedy Lewis Capital Partners Master Fund III LP and parallel vehicles) and KLRES (Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company LP).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024 (filed 2025-03), Item 1 Business / Our Manager

facts.fact: Platform: Kennedy Lewis runs an in-house land-banking servicer / asset-management division that monitors horizontal development pace and community sales, handles capital disbursements, homesite sales and monthly option-payment collection, and supports diligence. The FY2024 10-K says it is led by David Valiaveedan and staffed by people who worked at Lennar, Hovnanian, Beazer, Toll Brothers, Woodbridge Builders and the land-banking platforms of DW Partners and Blackstone Credit; the Manager's underwriting team has more than 30 diligence professionals.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024 (filed 2025-03), Item 1 Business / Our Manager

facts.fact: In August 2024 Kennedy Lewis added 12 people from Gibraltar Real Estate Capital (a residential development capital provider) and folded them into KL Servicers, its unit for asset monitoring, servicing and diligence on land-banking investments. Gibraltar co-founders Roger Brush and Michael Lapat joined as managing directors; they had executed about $3.5 billion of transactions across 25 states. The firm was put at $16 billion AUM in the article.
facts.source_title: Alternatives Watch, 2024-08-14

facts.fact: Kennedy Lewis describes the product as 'homebuilder finance': structured capital for US homebuilders to buy land and complete horizontal development capital-efficiently and relieve balance-sheet pressure. Its flagship opportunistic credit fund (Fund III) carries exposure to the strategy alongside its other credit verticals.
facts.source_title: Kennedy Lewis press release 2023-11-07 (PR Newswire)

facts.fact: Kennedy Lewis built its homebuilder-finance / land-banking strategy by hiring David Valiaveedan and Brieanne Nikrandt as Managing Directors on 2021-06-28 'to lead the firm's homebuilder financing strategy'. Both came from DW Partners, where they had led residential investments since 2015; Valiaveedan formed and led DW's Domain Real Estate Partners and was earlier VP Finance & Treasurer of Hovnanian. Kennedy Lewis had about $7 billion of AUM at the time.
facts.source_title: Kennedy Lewis press release 2021-06-28 (PR Newswire)

facts.fact: EDGAR shows only two filings for KLRES (Form D 2023-10-10 and D/A 2024-10-11) as of 2026-11-19: no 2025 or 2026 amendment. Inferred (from the absence of the annual amendment an ongoing offering requires): the KLRES offering probably stopped taking new money before October 2025; final size not disclosed.
facts.source_title: SEC EDGAR submissions listing, CIK 1995205

facts.fact: On the Q3 2026 call management said the fee is 1.25% of gross tangible assets excluding the new single-family-rental portfolio: Kennedy Lewis proposed leaving SFR homes out of the fee base while the product is unproven, and acknowledged that the $250 million buyback shrinks its own fee base.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

facts.fact: A third-party Form ADV aggregator lists KLRES at $886.8 million gross asset value, 103 beneficial owners, $10 million minimum investment, adviser Kennedy Lewis Management LP, auditor Deloitte, administrator HedgeServ, custodian JPMorgan (page shows data through Oct 2026; exact Form ADV date not shown).
facts.source_title: PrivateFundData.com profile of Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company LP

facts.fact: Millrose management fee expense was $30.264 million for Q3 2026 (Q3 2025: $25.895 million) and $88.325 million for the nine months to 2026-09-30 (2025: $59.959 million). Inferred run-rate: about $121 million a year (Q3 x 4).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations

facts.fact: Across five Fund IV vehicles filed 2026-09-21 (Domestic $1.46bn, Co-Inv Domestic $319.1m, Offshore $248.3m, USTE $146.1m, Co-Inv USTE $23.0m) about $2.19 billion had been sold, per a trade summary of the Form Ds. Fund IV is the successor to Fund III and may allocate to land banking.
facts.source_title: Angellinx market insights, 2026-09-22

facts.fact: Fund IV: KLCP Domestic Fund IV LP Form D/A signed 2026-09-21 shows a $4.5 billion total offering, $1,456.4 million sold to 40 investors, first sale 2024-12-31; placement agents PJT Partners, Rockefeller Capital Management and Cleopatra Consulting UK. This is the main domestic vehicle only.
facts.source_title: Form D/A, KLCP Domestic Fund IV LP (filed 2026-09-21)

facts.fact: 2026-08-27 amendment to the management agreement: property-level operating costs of single-family rental homes became a Millrose-paid 'Reimbursable Expense' (the Manager still bears other operating expenses), and the investment guidelines were restated to cover homesites for single-family detached/attached homes including homes held as rentals under an approved SFR strategy. Signed for both sides by Robert Nitkin.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Millrose Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27, 8-K Ex. 10.2 (restated Exhibit C Allocation Policy)

facts.fact: Lennar and the Manager: no Lennar equity stake in the Manager is disclosed. Lennar instead holds contractual consent rights under the Founder's Rights Agreement over any successor manager or management agreement, over replacement of the key men (Chene and Richman), and over transfers of Manager membership interests to homebuilders. After its Oct-Nov 2025 exchange offer Lennar held only a de minimis amount of Millrose stock.
facts.source_title: Millrose DEF 14A filed 2026-04-02

facts.fact: Ownership: the 2026 proxy lists no Kennedy Lewis entity among 5% holders of Millrose. Darren Richman beneficially owned 265,000 Class A shares (under 1%) as of 2026-03-23. Certain Millrose officers have ownership and financial interests in Kennedy Lewis.
facts.source_title: Millrose DEF 14A filed 2026-04-02

facts.fact: Latest firm AUM in a primary source: 'in excess of $33.0 billion' as of 2025-12-31, including Millrose at its gross assets (AUM method varies by fund and counts commitments).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 / Item 1A

facts.fact: Millrose paid the Kennedy Lewis manager about $87.8 million of management fee for 2025.
facts.source_title: Millrose DEF 14A filed 2026-04-02

facts.fact: Earlier firm AUM points: over $25 billion including Millrose as of 2025-03-25 (funded and unfunded commitments), per the Millrose FY2024 10-K. Other releases cited in this file give about $7bn (June 2021), about $14bn (Nov 2023), $16bn (Aug 2024, trade press) and about $30bn (July 2025, Taylor Morrison release).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024 (filed 2025-03), Item 1 Business / Our Manager

facts.fact: Fee from Millrose: 1.25% a year of Tangible Assets (0.3125% a quarter, paid in advance), payable regardless of performance; the Manager pays Millrose's ordinary operating costs and officer compensation out of the fee. Initial term three years from 2025-02-07 with one-year renewals; termination fee is 3.0x average annual fee if 3-year average ROE is at least 7%, otherwise 2.5x (accelerated) or 1.5x (at expiry).
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

facts.fact: The management agreement treats an assignment to a homebuilder or homesite developer, or certain changes of control involving David K. Chene or Darren L. Richman, as an assignment of the agreement (i.e. needing consent).
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

facts.fact: KLRES Form D/A (signed 2024-10-10): $724.7 million sold ($724,737,665) to 79 investors, offering still indefinite, PJT Partners LP named as placement agent, signed by Anthony Pasqua as authorized signatory.
facts.source_title: Form D/A, Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co LP (filed 2024-10-11)

facts.fact: Petershill (Goldman Sachs Asset Management) made a strategic investment in Kennedy Lewis, referenced by Alternatives Watch in Aug 2024 as 'recent'; Richman tied the Gibraltar team hire to growth after that investment. Stake size not found. The exact announcement date (2024-04-02) was seen only in a search-result headline, not opened.
facts.source_title: Alternatives Watch, 2024-08-14

facts.fact: Fund III: Kennedy Lewis Capital Partners Master Fund III LP and parallel / co-investment vehicles closed at $4.1 billion on 2023-11-07 against a $3 billion target, about 50% deployed at close; investors are pensions, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, foundations and endowments. Fund III is a named 'Priority Account' for land banking under the Millrose allocation policy.
facts.source_title: Kennedy Lewis press release 2023-11-07 (PR Newswire)

facts.fact: Dedicated land vehicle: Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co LP ('KLRES', Delaware LP formed 2023, GP Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company GP LLC). Original Form D (signed 2023-10-04): first sale 2023-10-02, $410.0 million sold to 3 investors, offering size indefinite, exemptions 506(b) and 3(c)(1)/3(c)(7).
facts.source_title: Form D, Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co LP (filed 2023-10-10)

facts.fact: Positioning of private capital against Millrose: on the Q3 2026 call management said no Kennedy Lewis-managed vehicle outside Millrose took part in the roughly $1.1 billion Dream Finders / Beazer financing, and Richman pointed to Kennedy Lewis's access to 'hundreds of blue chip LPs'. Millrose then had 22 counterparties.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

facts.fact: Restated allocation policy (2026-08-27): Priority Accounts are now any Kennedy Lewis-managed entity allocating capital to land banking (Fund III and KLRES and their affiliated/successor vehicles are named). The terms 'Overflow Funds' and '$1B Allocation' no longer appear. The ban on raising outside land-banking capital now applies only 'as long as Millrose has Available Capital'; Fund IV and KLRES (and successors) may raise without board consent; new successor funds and new land-banking-focused vehicles count as Priority Accounts in the rotation. Reading the two versions side by side is this agent's comparison: confirm in the exhibit.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Millrose Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27, 8-K Ex. 10.2 (restated Exhibit C Allocation Policy)

facts.fact: Under both versions Millrose's 'Available Capital' excludes capital subject to Lennar's Capital Priority Right, the rotation ends when the private accounts' investment periods end (then everything goes to Millrose if it has capital), and the Manager reports rotation and follow-on allocations to the Millrose board each quarter.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Millrose Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27, 8-K Ex. 10.2 (restated Exhibit C Allocation Policy)

facts.fact: Counterparty change: Taylor Morrison, Kennedy Lewis's largest disclosed non-Lennar builder relationship ($3 billion Yardly facility plus a for-sale land bank), was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway on 2026-07-24 for $72.50 a share in cash and has delisted. The 8-K does not mention the Kennedy Lewis facilities.
facts.source_title: Taylor Morrison 8-K filed 2026-07-24 (merger closing)

facts.fact: In the Landsea deal the commitment was signed by Kennedy Lewis Investment Management, LLC 'and/or its affiliates' (Darren Richman, authorized signatory) with no fund named; the funding was then placed in Millrose, which provided more than $500 million. This is the 'manager commits, then allocates' pattern a rival will meet.
facts.source_title: Cox, Castle & Nicholson deal announcement, 2025-07-21

facts.fact: Original allocation policy (2025-02-07): 'Priority Accounts' were Fund III (incl. KLIM Delta HQ3 LP and Kennedy Lewis Capital Partners (EU) SPV LP) and KLRES. Deals directed to Millrose by Lennar or a builder went 100% to Millrose; follow-ons on existing Kennedy Lewis land banks could go 100% to the private funds; all other deals suitable for both alternated on a rotation starting with Millrose. 'Overflow Funds' got deals only if neither Millrose nor a Priority Account had capital. A builder could opt out in writing ('Non-Millrose Deal').
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

facts.fact: Original fundraising limit (2025-02-07): without Millrose board approval Kennedy Lewis could not raise capital for land banking outside Millrose, except Overflow Funds and a '$1B Allocation': Fund IV could raise freely but only up to $1 billion of it could go to land banking as a rotation participant.
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

builder_relationships.description: Land-banking partnership with Kennedy Lewis began in 2021 (private funds, before Millrose); Millrose's investor presentation is quoted as citing '$4.5B+' of land-banking transactions between Lennar and Kennedy Lewis since 2022. Kennedy Lewis then advised Lennar on structuring Millrose and was chosen as its manager without a competitive process. Deal-level lots and yields for the pre-Millrose land banks are not public.

$3 billion land and construction financing facility with Kennedy Lewis Investment Management for the Yardly build-to-rent brand, announced 2025-07-23: funds existing and new land, land development and vertical construction; pitched as balance-sheet relief and flexibility on later asset sales. Rate, term and which Kennedy Lewis vehicle funds it are not disclosed (the Millrose Q3 2026 call refers to it as prior Millrose-related activity). Taylor Morrison has been owned by Berkshire Hathaway since 2026-07-24.

Kennedy Lewis-managed Millrose funded about $1.1 billion for Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes (closed 2026-10-20): about $580 million of land banking net of option deposits on roughly 7,000 homesites, plus about $488 million of preferred stock (12% dividend, net of OID). No Kennedy Lewis private vehicle participated.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

builder_relationships.builder_name: The New Home Company (now Risewell Homes)
builder_relationships.description: Kennedy Lewis Investment Management committed 100% of a land bank facility of up to $700 million on 2025-05-12 ($600 million at closing, $100 million for later horizontal development) to fund New Home's acquisition of Landsea Homes: pooled option agreements, 72-month maximum option term, takedown price at least 105.25% of closing commitment, fees in an unfiled fee letter. Deal closed 2025-06-25.
builder_relationships.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

builder_relationships.builder_name: The New Home Company (now Risewell Homes) / Landsea Homes
builder_relationships.description: Funding of the above landed in Millrose: Millrose provided more than $500 million from the land banking facility across properties in five states, alongside Apollo fund equity and New Home senior notes; described as the first use of land-bank proceeds at this scale to buy a public builder.

Pre-existing land banking agreement with Kennedy Lewis serving Taylor Morrison's for-sale homebuilding, referenced in the July 2025 release. Start date, size, lots and pricing are not disclosed; Taylor Morrison's FY2025 10-K (parts read) does not name its land bankers.

Land banking facility 'established by JPI and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management' for Class A multifamily sites, funded through Millrose: Millrose buys sites and funds development, JPI pays option fees and takes sites down as its pipeline matures. First acquisition closed by 2026-07-30; facility size not disclosed. First Kennedy Lewis land bank outside for-sale housing.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose/JPI press release 2026-07-30 (Business Wire copy on Yahoo Finance)

gaps: Web search budget for this session ran out part-way through: builder-by-builder searches were run once as a combined query (Landsea, Dream Finders, United Homes Group, Smith Douglas, Hovnanian, Century Communities, LGI, M/I, Meritage, KB Home, Tri Pointe, Beazer) and returned no Kennedy Lewis private land-bank deals; individual per-builder searches and builder 10-K text searches were NOT completed. Treat absence as 'not found', not 'does not exist'.

Total size of Kennedy Lewis's private land-banking book (dollars deployed, lots, number of builders): not publicly disclosed. Only data points: KLRES $724.7m sold by Oct 2024 / $886.8m gross assets per ADV aggregator; Fund III $4.1bn (land share undisclosed); '$4.5B+' with Lennar since 2022 (secondary).

KLRES final close size, investment period end date and any KLRES II / successor vehicle: not found on EDGAR (no Form D after Oct 2024). The investment-period end matters because the Millrose rotation stops when the Priority Accounts' investment periods end.

Yields, option fees, deposits and minimum returns Kennedy Lewis charges builders in private funds: not public. The New Home fee letter was not filed; Taylor Morrison's filings (FY2025 10-K sections read) do not name Kennedy Lewis or give land-banker rates. Taylor Morrison stopped SEC reporting in Aug 2026.

Taylor Morrison for-sale land banking agreement with Kennedy Lewis: start date, capacity, lots not disclosed. Split of the $3bn Yardly facility between Millrose and Kennedy Lewis private funds: not found.

How the private land strategy is financed (fund-level credit lines, back-leverage, securitisations, insurance capital, rated notes): nothing public found for Fund III/KLRES. Millrose's own debt is covered by the Millrose team.

Lennar ownership stake in the Manager: none disclosed in the management agreement or 2026 proxy (consent rights only). Kennedy Lewis entity-level holding of MRP shares: none shown at 5%+; exact holding not disclosed.

kennedylewis.com (team page, AUM, news) could not be opened: domain safety check rate-limited, /team returned 404. Current titles of Valiaveedan, Nikrandt, Brush and Lapat therefore rest on 2021-2025 sources. LinkedIn not used.

Unopened 2026 leads seen only in search snippets (not recorded as facts): reports that Kennedy Lewis explored a sale of the firm (The Middle Market, 403); Greenbrier resort joint venture (Aug 2026); Bank of Ireland EUR 2bn lending partnership (Mar 2026).
